channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Seven months of checks: what is known about the incident with a journalist at the Osh Internal Affairs Department
item.description: An investigation into an incident involving journalist Nurzhamal Ganieva at the Osh Internal Affairs Department has been ongoing for over seven months. Investigators have thrice refused to open a criminal case, with prosecutors overturning each decision. Other state bodies found violations in emergency reporting and medical documentation of violence.

item.title: Tajikistan and Austria Sign Agreement to Modernize Glacier Meteorological Station
item.description: Tajikistan's Hydrometeorology Agency and Austria's Institute of Science and Technology have signed a cooperation agreement to modernize the Gorbunova meteorological station on the 'Tajikistan' glacier. The pact aims to enhance research on glaciers, cryosphere, hydrology, meteorology, and climate change.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New Rules for Anti-Corruption Checks in Government Bodies
item.description: Uzbekistan has established unified procedures for anti-corruption inspections within state bodies and organizations. Compliance and internal control units will conduct these checks to identify and prevent corruption risks. The frequency of checks depends on the assessed risk level.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce 300% Surcharge for Psychologists Starting January 1
item.description: Starting January 1, psychologists and social workers in Kazakhstan will see a salary increase. A draft government resolution proposes a surcharge of 300% for psychologists and 200% for social workers in primary healthcare organizations, based on their length of service. This aims to compensate for psycho-emotional and physical strain.

item.title: Over One Billion People Worldwide Suffer from Iron Deficiency, Euronews Reports
item.description: More than a billion people globally suffer from iron deficiency, often undiagnosed due to symptoms mimicking other illnesses, according to Euronews. Iron is crucial for hemoglobin production, oxygen transport, muscle function, and energy. Severe deficiency can lead to iron-deficiency anemia, impacting quality of life.

item.title: Nearly 300 Million Tenge Stolen in Kazakhstan Science Development Scheme
item.description: Authorities in Astana have uncovered a scheme to embezzle over 297 million tenge from a state grant for commercializing scientific research. An individual entrepreneur allegedly misused funds intended for a plant oil regeneration project. The Anti-Corruption Agency reported that equipment was not purchased as specified, and no products were manufactured.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Security Committee Seizes 45 Firearms and Ammunition
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) reported the seizure of 45 firearms, 10 grenades, and over 1200 rounds of ammunition in Shymkent and 10 regions. The operation, conducted in October-November, aimed to curb illegal arms trafficking. Pre-trial investigations are underway for the discovered violations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Egg Production Surges 20.8%, Meat Up 4.1%, Milk Up 2.3% in Jan-Oct
item.description: In January-October 2026, Kyrgyzstan's egg production increased by 20.8% year-on-year, the highest growth among livestock products. Meat production rose 4.1%, milk 2.3%, and wool 0.5%. Crop production also saw significant growth, with barley up 45.3% and wheat up 44.9%.

item.title: Almaty Bans New Construction Near Rivers and Lakes in Water Protection Zones
item.description: A new decree in Almaty prohibits construction within 35 meters of rivers, streams, canals, and lakes. Wider protection zones, ranging from 120 to 500 meters, require projects to be approved by government bodies. The decree covers 32 water bodies, including the Malaya Almatinka River and Big Almaty Lake.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Anti-Corruption Agency Uncovers Embezzlement Scheme at Science Fund
item.description: Kazakhstan's Agency for Financial Monitoring (AFM) has exposed an embezzlement scheme involving the Science Fund. The company Bal halal reportedly received 1.15 billion tenge in 2023-2024 for the production of 'innovative pasta,' but the funds were allegedly misappropriated.

item.title: Astana Businessman Suspected of Embezzling Nearly 300 Million Tenge from Science Fund Grant
item.description: A businessman in Astana is suspected of embezzling nearly 300 million tenge from a grant provided by the Science Fund. The funds were intended for a project on regenerating and purifying vegetable oils. The suspect allegedly diverted money through controlled companies, purchasing substandard equipment and not producing the promised goods. The estimated damage exceeds 297 million tenge.

item.title: Osh Announces Tender for Management of Municipal Car Market
item.description: Osh has announced an open tender for the temporary management of its municipal car market. The market is currently managed by a contractor who renovated it, and to whom the mayor's office owes approximately 380 million soms. The city needs funds for other urgent needs, so the market will be temporarily managed by the contractor to recoup renovation costs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Launch Pilot Project for Air Ticket Seller Registration
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will introduce mandatory registration for companies and individuals selling air tickets. A 11-month pilot project will test the new mechanism, affecting ticket agencies and travel agents. The government aims to regulate the market, improve service quality, provide accurate information, and enhance consumer protection. The State Agency for Civil Aviation is responsible for implementation.

item.title: Astana: Embezzlement of grant funds totaling over 297 million tenge uncovered
item.description: Authorities in Astana have uncovered a scheme to embezzle state grant funds allocated for the commercialization of scientific developments. Two suspects have been detained. The investigation revealed that a private entrepreneur received a grant for a vegetable oil processing project but purchased substandard equipment, causing losses exceeding 297 million tenge.

item.title: Kazakhstan Health Ministry Proposes 300% Salary Bonus for Psychologists
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has proposed a draft resolution to increase salaries for primary healthcare specialists. Psychologists working in polyclinics could receive a 300% bonus to their base salary, and social workers 200%. These measures aim to retain staff and improve access to medical care, with salary increases set for January 1, 2027.

item.title: Expert: Individual Approach Needed for Each Child in Inclusive Education
item.description: An expert emphasized the importance of considering individual needs for every child with special developmental needs in inclusive education. Victoria Toktosunova stated that beyond diagnosis, a child's unique characteristics, abilities, strengths, and weaknesses must be considered. Even children with the same diagnosis may require different support.

item.title: Former Afghan President Karzai Urges Unrestricted Access to Education for All Children
item.description: On International Children's Day, former Afghan President Hamid Karzai stressed the need for unrestricted access to education for all children, boys and girls. He highlighted that millions of Afghan children face severe malnutrition and are deprived of primary education, emphasizing education's role in national development and security.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Chemical Industry Surges 2.4 Times, Base Metals Output Drops 6.1%
item.description: In January-October 2026, Kyrgyzstan's chemical production output increased 2.4 times year-on-year. Refined petroleum products rose 1.8 times, and vehicles by 38.3%. Overall industrial production grew 5.2%. However, base metals output decreased by 6.1%, attributed to planned production cuts at the Kumtor mine.

item.title: CNPC Subsidiary KMK-Munai Considers Delisting from Kazakhstan Stock Exchange
item.description: KMK-Munai, a subsidiary of China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC), is considering delisting its shares from the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE). The decision will be put to an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders on December 11. The company reported a profit of 5.2 billion tenge for 2025.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Deposits Grow by 62 Billion Som in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: Deposits held by individuals in Kyrgyzstan's commercial banks and credit organizations increased by approximately 62.4 billion som from January to September 2026, reaching a total of 425.4 billion som. This represents a 17.2% rise in citizen savings over the nine-month period. Commercial banks hold the majority of these funds.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Processed Agricultural Exports Increase by Nearly $1 Billion
item.description: The value of processed agricultural product exports from Kazakhstan has grown by almost $1 billion. This significant increase indicates a positive trend in the country's agricultural sector, suggesting enhanced production and international market competitiveness for its processed goods. Further details on specific products and markets were not provided.

item.title: Kazakhstan Parliament Speaker Meets Turkmenistan's Mejlis Chairman
item.description: Aibek Dadebay, Chairman of the Mejlis of Kazakhstan, met with Dunyagozel Gulmanova, Chairperson of the Mejlis of Turkmenistan, on the sidelines of the 61st plenary session of the CIS Parliamentary Assembly Council. Dadebay congratulated Turkmenistan on becoming an observer in the CIS PA and praised its initiative to strengthen UN-CIS ties. He highlighted the strong strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan, emphasizing cooperation in energy, agriculture, healthcare, and transport.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Freight and Passenger Transport Sees Significant Growth
item.description: In January-October 2026, Kyrgyzstan's freight transport volume reached 60.7 million tons, a 9.4% increase year-on-year. Passenger transport carried 577.1 million people, up 8.3%. The transport and warehousing services sector grew by 4.5% to 118.7 billion soms. Overall, the services sector expanded by 6.4% to 1.43 trillion soms during the same period.

item.title: US War Against Iran Costs Over $48 Billion Since February
item.description: The US military operation against Iran has cost over $48.3 billion as of November 13 since the conflict began in late February, according to Pentagon budget official Arthur Miller. The expenses include munitions, equipment replacement, and operational costs. Miller could not provide data on damage to US military facilities during the war, which began February 28 with strikes on Iran and retaliatory attacks.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Reduce Unemployment Benefit Duration to Three Months by 2027
item.description: Starting in 2027, Kazakhstan will limit unemployment benefits to a maximum of three months, down from six. The maximum benefit amount will increase to 346,500 tenge, calculated as 45% of the average earnings over the past two years. Job seekers must register at a career center for up to 13 days before eligibility.

item.title: Uzbekistan Rises 31 Places in UN E-Government Development Index to 32nd
item.description: Uzbekistan has climbed 31 places to rank 32nd out of 194 countries in the UN E-Government Development Index 2026. The country entered the 'Very High EGDI' category for the first time. Uzbekistan now ranks 9th among Asian nations and 2nd in Central Asia, with an EGDI score of 0.8930.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Jordan Foster Closer Ties Between Central Asia and the Middle East
item.description: Uzbekistan and Jordan are enhancing their partnership, focusing on industrial cooperation, technological development, and preserving shared spiritual heritage. High-level political will from both leaders has significantly boosted relations since diplomatic ties were established in 1993. A state visit by King Abdullah II in August 2025 marked a transition to comprehensive partnership.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seizes 45 Firearms and 1,259 Rounds of Ammunition in Illegal Circulation
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee, in cooperation with police, conducted operations across 10 regions and Shymkent, seizing 45 illegal firearms, including assault rifles, rifles, and pistols, along with 10 grenades and 1,259 rounds of ammunition. Pre-trial investigations are underway for these cases.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Expands Fuel Subsidies to Include ECO-93 Gasoline
item.description: The Kyrgyz Cabinet has included ECO-93 gasoline in its fuel subsidy program to stabilize market prices. Diesel fuel for "Kyrgyzkomur" has been set at 92.85 som per liter. These measures aim to control costs for coal extraction and transportation, preventing price hikes for consumers.

item.title: Illegal Fishing of Red Book Fish in Uzbekistan Causes Over 1 Billion Som Damage
item.description: Two individuals in Uzbekistan's Namangan region were caught illegally fishing 31 fish, including 8 endangered Turkestan barbel, using prohibited electric fishing gear. The environmental damage is estimated at over 1 billion Uzbek som. Authorities have initiated legal proceedings.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Launch Direct Flights to Tokyo, Seoul, and Singapore
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is planning to open direct flights to Tokyo, Seoul, and Singapore. The Director of the State Agency for Tourism Development, Eduard Kubatov, stated that discussions are also underway for routes to Frankfurt, Munich, Prague, Milan, London, and Budapest. Asman Airlines aims to launch international flights with new aircraft by 2027.

item.title: Kylym Bank and StoneX Group Sign Memorandum of Cooperation
item.description: Kylym Bank and the Singapore office of the international financial group StoneX Group have signed a memorandum of understanding. The agreement aims to foster long-term strategic cooperation, focusing on international capital markets, currency operations, precious metals trading, and attracting foreign investors to Kyrgyzstan's financial market.

item.title: Public Hearings Scheduled for Almaty Waste Incinerator Construction
item.description: Public hearings have been scheduled for the construction of a waste incinerator in Almaty. The event will allow citizens to voice their opinions and concerns regarding the project.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Education Ministry Ready to Address Private Education Sector Issues
item.description: The Ministry of Education in Kyrgyzstan is open to dialogue to resolve issues faced by private schools and kindergartens. The ministry stated that efforts are underway to simplify licensing procedures and digitize the education sector, making it easier for private institutions to operate.

item.title: Afghan Foreign Ministry Spokesperson: US War in Afghanistan Driven by Geopolitics, Not 9/11
item.description: Abdul Qahar Balkhi, spokesperson for Afghanistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, stated that the US-led war was driven by geopolitical and strategic interests, not primarily the 9/11 attacks. He argued Afghanistan's location made it strategically important to the US after the Soviet Union's collapse, aiming to expand global influence.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Stricter Controls on Charitable Fundraising to Combat Fraud
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering new regulations for charitable collections to protect citizens from fraudsters who solicit funds for sick children or other social causes but misuse them. The proposed bill aims to update the 1999 law, which does not account for modern online donation methods. It introduces concepts like public charitable collection, organizer registration, and dedicated bank accounts.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Halyk Bank Offers Integrated Mortgage Solution via SuperApp
item.description: Halyk Bank in Kazakhstan has launched a new feature in its SuperApp, allowing customers to select developers and residential complexes for mortgage applications. This partnership program includes major developers like BI Group and covers properties in Almaty, Astana, Shymkent, and Atyrau, simplifying the home-buying process by integrating property search and mortgage application.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Significant Bonuses for Psychologists and Social Workers
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has proposed new bonuses for psychologists and social workers in primary healthcare, effective January 1, 2027. Psychologists could receive up to 300% of their base salary, and social workers up to 200%, to reduce staff turnover and shortages.

item.title: Russian President Putin Arrives in Tajikistan After China Visit
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, following a visit to Shenzhen, China. He was welcomed by Tajik President Emomali Rahmon. The leaders are expected to discuss bilateral issues. The visit follows a previous invitation by Rahmon during a CIS summit in Moscow, where time constraints limited discussions.

item.title: Tajikistan and Russia Expand Cooperation in Land Management
item.description: Tajikistan hosted a working meeting between its State Committee for Land Management and Geodesy and a delegation of experts from Russia's Federal Service for State Registration, Cadastre, and Cartography. The visit aimed to strengthen bilateral cooperation in land resource management, real estate registration, cadastral accounting, geodesy, and cartography.
